title: Windowed capacity mapping and rapid-scope snap for cycle anchoring
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Create a lightweight, repeatable 'windowed capacity map' and a 'rapid scope snap' process to anchor cycles against variable staffing and emergent priorities. Motivation: current cycle planning relies on large tranche commitments and manual re-slicing which adds friction mid-cycle. The windowed approach breaks the cycle into 2-3 cascading time windows (anchor window, flex window, reserve window) with clear staffing commitments and a compact decision protocol for scope snaps (fast, surgical scope cuts) when capacity shifts.

Deliverables:
- Confluence PRD describing windows, role-band definitions, and escalation thresholds (link below).
- Spreadsheet capacity model (per-role, per-window) and a lightweight UI template for Console leads to visualize window capacity.
- Playbook doc for PMs and Eng leads with step-by-step scope snap checklist and communication templates.
- Pilot run with 2 initiatives during 2025-W09 to validate flow and metrics.

Success metrics:
- Reduced mid-cycle scope churn: aim for >=30% fewer unplanned scope drops during pilot.
- Faster decision latency: median scope-snap decision time <= 6 hours for minor scope snaps.
- Predictability: forecast variance (planned vs actual FTE-days) reduced by 20% across pilot teams.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- Trade off fine-grained accuracy for speed; models will use role-level buckets rather than task-level estimates.
- Requires cultural adoption of stricter anchoring; risk of over-trimming. Pilot will include guardrails (review board, stakeholder opt-out).

Artifacts:
- PRD (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/CYC/Windowed+Capacity+Map+PRD
- Model sheet (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b_windowed_capacity_model
- Pilot brief & signoff form: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1pilot-brief
- Visualization mock (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/Windowed-Map-Mock
